gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: A narrow slit nearly shuts the c in Groovy, whose loose lowercase has funky, friendly swagger. Noto Sans Myanmar settles underneath as a dense, heavy-looking band of text with a broad, welcoming c, so a long read feels sturdy and clean.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Groovy puts a friendly, funky face forward, with flat, contrast-free letterforms and arms of constant width. And Noto Sans Nabataean follows with lowercase standing almost cap-tall and wide-open s curves, so extended reading stays contemporary and easy on the eye.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-nag-munda: Closed, slit-like curves give Groovy its funky bounce. Noto Sans Nag Mundari answers with half-unwrapped c and s shapes and lowercase rivaling the capitals, so paragraphs run on in a contemporary, open sans voice.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-nandinaga: Noto Sans Nandinagari reads approachably, with generous openings at every weight, short ascenders and a big lowercase body. Under Groovy's thin-looking, uniform strokes, paragraphs stay mellow.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-newa: Groovy's letters look drawn with a round-tipped pen, narrow slits almost closing the c, with a loose, funky stride. Against its closed shapes, Noto Sans Newa brings a clearly open e, the plain sans opposite.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu has a towering x-height and terminals held far from the stroke body, which makes it feel modern and spacious. Groovy's closed, contrast-free letters sit above it, giving the page a snug top and open bottom.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham reads clean and contemporary, with wide gaps in the e and tall bodies that make the lowercase look bold. Groovy's fixed-nib strokes and friendly slits sit above it, a tight heading over open plain sans.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Friendly and funky, Groovy narrows its c to a slit. Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds its curve tails well back, so words form solid blocks, and the plain sans makes the strongest foil to those closed shapes.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-old-hunga: Funky, loose and cheerful, Groovy keeps every stroke width constant from stem to curve, its c nearly sealed. Noto Sans Old Hungarian opens large counters in a, e and s, a plain sans that stays legible at tiny sizes.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-old-itali: Noto Sans Old Italic reads contemporary, with hardly any gap between x-height and cap height and curve endings kept well apart. And Groovy's closed, friendly letters, free of pinched joins, give way to that sans-serif's open, steady texture.
